findings.description: send_campaign only catches RecipientRefused. Any other mailer failure (connection error, timeout, SMTP server disconnect) or a render error such as a KeyError/IndexError from body_template.format propagates out of the loop. The caller then gets no CampaignReport, so it cannot tell who was already sent the campaign. A retry would re-send to everyone who succeeded, because there is no record of them.
findings.suggestion: Catch other exceptions per recipient and record them (e.g. a `failed` dict), or attach the partial report to the exception, so the caller can resume without duplicate sends.
findings.title: A non-RecipientRefused error aborts the whole send and discards the report

findings.description: In eligible(), an address is added to `seen` only after the confirmed/unsubscribed/list checks pass. Because the dedup key is the lowercased, stripped email, an ineligible record does not block a later record for the same address. Records for the same address with different state therefore make delivery depend on input order, which is a policy question rather than a clear bug. The more concrete issue is in send_campaign, where `report.sent` and `report.refused` use the raw `subscriber.email` rather than the normalized address, so reports can contain case or whitespace variants of the same address.
findings.suggestion: Use a normalized address consistently as the key for dedup, sending and reporting.
findings.title: Dedup marks address as seen only after eligibility checks, so later duplicate can slip through
